top_choice_rationale: Mircea Cărtărescu is the only writer on the slate, and I judge him on the common criteria rather than on the identical opening rankings. His voice is recognizable at the level of the sentence and of the whole book. Blinding and Solenoid, as publicly known, build memory, the body, dream and cosmology into very large structures, which suggests formal ambition and imaginative depth. Solenoid appears to be a different construction rather than a copy of the earlier trilogy, and the oeuvre also includes poetry and shorter prose, so a whole-oeuvre citation is plausible. The citation should name Romanian prose with poetry as its ground and describe what the writing does, without national or regional symbolism. Caveats: I cannot assess Romanian rhythm and long-sentence control, translation may flatten them, and the late volumes may be uneven. Poetry and essays are thinly covered in translation, and I have not independently verified any source. The reading of the will's idealistic tendency remains open, and I would not use it to exclude an inward or disturbing project. Awarding the prize is preferable to no award, since no round-2 evidence undermines the case.
